topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the core learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancers develop through genetic mutations and permissive microenvironments, influenced by inherited predisposition, environmental exposures, and global demographic patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of biological, physical, and chemical carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specific molecular mechanisms by which infectious agents, radiation, and chemical exposures act as tumor initiators or promoters to induce malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and assess exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding summary and final takeaways of the lecture.
